name: Hélène — strong XC pilot whose collapse response is still untested
summary: Over 200 hours with 60-odd thermic, flying weekly on proper thermic days, confident thermalling in a busy climb, reliable launches, good descent options, and clear evidence the wing is holding her back. Last season she took a big collapse, froze, and the wing recovered on its own. She knows the theory and hasn't practised it since.
why_this_persona: The borderline single-weak-check case, and the distinction that matters most in this rubric: freezing in a collapse trips a Ready-blocker, losing control of the wing trips a gate. She sits one band above the gate. She also carries this step's strongest claim on the manoeuvres-course suggestion — two instructors argue independently that the wing she owns now is close to the last one a collapse can be induced on realistically.

notes: Computed skills 84.8, psychological 95.1, total 89.4, no bonus. A high score held at Nearly ready by one answer, which is the behaviour the single-answer blockers exist to produce.

ORDER CHECK: her collapse_practice answer ('theory only', 0.3) would also fail the floor, but collapse_experience comes first in thresholds.ready.critical_check_floor.questions, and the engine breaks on the first failure. So exactly one rule string is emitted and it names collapse_experience. A scorer that emits both, or that names collapse_practice, has either lost the break or changed the list order — both worth catching, because the list order is deliberate (most-to-least step-specific) and the message the pilot sees depends on it.

'collapse_control_lost' must NOT fire. She froze and the wing recovered itself, which is one band above the two answers that gate. That distinction is the single most important boundary in this rubric's collapse handling, and persona 08 is the only persona sitting on it. A synthetic unit check should confirm that 'lost_control' and 'repeated_struggle' both cap at Not yet.

Both collapse suggestions fire alongside 'post_collapse_support', on three distinct topics (collapse, collapse_training, incident), so all three can reach the displayed set. That is intended: debriefing what happened, practising the recovery, and considering a course are three different actions, and she needs all three.

'nerves_are_not_the_problem' must NOT fire. She froze in a collapse but answers 'heart rate goes up, but I carry on flying the wing' about rough air generally. Those are different questions and the rubric treats them separately — freezing once in a specific event is not the same as falling apart under load, and conflating them would both misdiagnose her and read as a judgement on her nerve.
'debrief_habit' must not fire: her incidents answer is the reflected-on one, which scores full marks. She has debriefed; what she hasn't done is practise.

TONE CHECK: the rule message for 'critical_check_floor:collapse_experience' opens by saying freezing is what most people do the first time. docs/design-context.md requires hesitation and fear responses to be treated as information rather than as defects, and this is the message most at risk of breaching that.
